_comment: Golden vectors for AP2's checkout_hash, the value that binds a Checkout
Mandate to the merchant's offer and a Payment Mandate to the same one.
checkout_jwt below is a stand-in for a merchant-signed Checkout JWT. Its
contents do not matter and are never read: the binding is a digest over
the compact serialisation as a string, which is what removes any need to
canonicalise the merchant's JSON.
Each digest is base64url of the hash of those ASCII bytes, unpadded, with
no algorithm prefix — not 'sha-256:...'. The prefixed form appears nowhere
in the specification and would be a different value.
Three algorithms are pinned because AP2 ties checkout_hash to the SD-JWT's
own _sd_alg rather than to a fixed algorithm. A verifier that hardcoded
sha-256 passes the first row and fails the other two, reporting a hash
mismatch — which reads as tampering rather than as the bug it is.
One digest, two claim names. The Checkout Mandate carries it as
checkout_hash and the Payment Mandate as transaction_id — AP2 names the
payment claim differently while defining it as the same hash of the same
checkout. The values below are therefore vectors for both mandates, and
an implementation that reproduces them under only one name has not
reproduced the binding that links the two.
These are reproducible by anyone: printf the checkout_jwt value into
sha256sum and base64url-encode the raw digest.
